purpose: Contract for the Teleon primitive/component assembly compiler: RAG retrieves ComponentCards, the LLM emits a constrained PipelinePlan, deterministic code validates contracts/policy/order and emits a locked execution manifest. The LLM is planner/explainer only; it never builds or executes arbitrary code. The platform is deterministic-first, not deterministic-only: nondeterministic enrichment/codegen may propose candidate primitives, mutations, templates, or PipelineIR patches, but proof/provenance/promotion decide trust.

research_sources.takeaway: Use an LLM to plan tasks and select existing models/tools by function description, but route execution through controlled orchestration rather than free-form code.
LLMs can produce modular programs over existing visual functions; Teleon should output constrained graph IR over primitives instead of source dumps.
Visual reasoning can be composed by generated Python over tools; Teleon keeps the composition idea but replaces arbitrary Python with validated component plans.

For video, an LLM can generate structured plans over scenes/entities/layouts before a downstream generator runs; for code, Teleon should generate plans over primitive contracts before a compiler runs.
API/tool calls improve when grounded in retrieved API metadata. Teleon applies this to ComponentCards over code primitives.
Tool-use datasets and search over tool metadata support tool selection; Teleon uses hybrid primitive search plus strict promotion gates.
Function calls can be compiled into a dependency graph for scheduling; Teleon's compiler derives topological order and later runtime DAGs.
High-level prompts can compose low-level robot APIs; Teleon generalizes this to code primitives with I/O contracts and proof gates.
Software catalogs organize components, APIs, resources, and systems; Teleon ComponentCards are the searchable primitive catalog layer.
Directed component graphs with explicit connections and pre-run checks are the right pipeline shape; Teleon adds strict primitive contracts and lockfiles.
Durable workflow execution and deterministic replay discipline are a strong runtime fit for long-running primitive graphs.
Schema/constraint unification plus policy evaluation should validate plans, component cards, runtime manifests, licenses, and side effects before execution.

ir_layers.rule: Capture goal, constraints, guardrails, context, input/output surfaces, privacy, license, runtime preference, and success metrics.
LLM may propose nodes, component ids, purposes, bindings, gates, and side-effect declarations only from retrieved candidates.
Only deterministic compiler output may be executed: resolved versions, ordered nodes, source digests, seed strategy, policy report, runtime target, and registry snapshot.

hybrid_lane_policy.principle: Every representation can carry deterministic evidence and nondeterministic candidate enrichment. The compiler tries deterministic search, graph checks, type checks, policy checks, and verified mutations first; unresolved gaps may route to LLM/codegen, but those outputs remain candidate-only until deterministic proof and promotion.

planner_laws: The LLM emits PipelinePlan JSON/objects, not arbitrary executable source.
The LLM may reference only ComponentCards returned by retrieval.
The compiler derives ordering from bindings and policy, not from LLM vibes.
The executor runs a lockfile, never the raw LLM response.
Generated adapters or new primitives are candidates only until proof and promotion.
Deterministic search/check/mutation lanes run before nondeterministic candidate generation.
LLM-enriched compact views, reranks, templates, primitive variants, and PipelineIR patches may be useful candidate evidence but cannot serve truth or execute without deterministic validation.
promotion_policy: A lockfile is runnable candidate evidence, not promoted truth. Promotion requires deterministic proof commands, execution logs, graph edges, dependency/license provenance, and owner/human approval where needed.
